title_en: How We Are to Work for Islam
body_ar:
بدأ الإسلام غريباً وسيعود غريباً كما بدأ، وقد زالت الغربة الأولى للإسلام ليحل محلها العز والظهور والتمكين، بعد جهد متواصل وعمل دءوب، تجلى في سيرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وفي سيرة أصحابه ومن بعدهم، ونحن اليوم نعيش غربة جديدة للإسلام، ولن تزول هذه الغربة عن الإسلام إلا بعمل متواصل وجهود متضافرة من جميع فئات المسلمين.
تشريف الله لهذه الأمة على سائر الأمم:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه، ومن اهتدى بهداه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن جميع المسلمين يعلمون أن الله سبحانه وتعالى خلقهم لحكمة واضحة بينها في كتابه، وشرع لهم شرائع هذا الدين الذي هو خير شرائعه، وضمنه خير كتبه، وأرسل إليهم خير رسله، فشرفهم بذلك على سائر الأمم، وجعلهم أمة وسطاً ليكونوا شهداء على الناس، وقد ثبت عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصحيحين أنه قال: إن هذه الأمة شهود عدول يوم القيامة، وإنه ما من نبي إلا يخاصم أمته في الملأ الأعلى، فيقال له: من يشهد لك؟ فيقول: محمد وأمته. حتى إن نوحاً يخاصم أمته في الملأ الأعلى فيقولون: ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير! فيقول: مكثت فيكم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاماً أدعوكم إلى الله. وهم ينكرون، فيقال: من يشهد لك؟ فيقول: محمد وأمته...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Islam began as a stranger and will return to being a stranger as it began. The first estrangement of Islam passed away and was replaced by honour, ascendancy and established strength — after continuous effort and unwearying work, which showed itself in the life of the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, and in the lives of his Companions and of those who came after them. Today we are living a new estrangement of Islam, and this estrangement will not pass away from Islam except through continuous work and the joined efforts of every section of the Muslims.

## God's ennobling of this community above all other communities

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: all Muslims know that God, glorified and exalted is He, created them for a clear purpose which He has set out in His Book; that He laid down for them the code of this religion, which is the best of His codes; that He placed within it the best of His books; and that He sent to them the best of His messengers, and by this ennobled them above all other communities and made them a middle community, that they might be witnesses over mankind.

It is established from the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, that he said: "This community are witnesses whose probity is accepted on the Day of Resurrection. There is no prophet but that he will dispute with his community in the highest assembly, and it will be said to him: who will testify for you? And he will say: Muhammad and his community. Even Noah will dispute with his community in the highest assembly, and they will say: no bearer of good news and no warner came to us! And he will say: I remained among you a thousand years less fifty, calling you to God. And they will deny it, and it will be said: who will testify for you? And he will say: Muhammad and his community" …

flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis in the middle of the hadith it is citing, before the community's testimony is explained and long before the question of the title — how we are to work for Islam — is reached. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/c-c-29.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

options: keep his attribution and grading exactly as given and add nothing
supply the collection, book and narrator

flags.note: The Sheikh's attribution is 'established … in the two Ṣaḥīḥs' and nothing more, and the English says exactly that. No narrator, no book reference and no further grading has been added, per style guide section 4. Two things a reviewer should know, recorded here and not written into the text: the wording as served is a paraphrase rather than a verbatim matn, and the clause 'I remained among you a thousand years less fifty' reproduces Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:14 inside the reported speech. Neither has been marked or corrected in the English.

flags.context: in the hadith, and earlier in the Sheikh's own sentence
flags.note: 'عدل' is the technical qualification of a witness whose testimony is admissible because his probity is established. 'Just witnesses' would read as a moral compliment and lose the legal force, which is the whole point of the passage.

translator_notes: One of a run of six records, IDs 701-706, in the written-da'wah section, all uploaded on 9 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-c-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

'التمكين' is rendered 'established strength' — the condition of being firmly set in place and able to act — rather than 'empowerment', which in English carries a modern political register the Arabic does not.
The English breaks the transcribed portion into two paragraphs where the source runs on, purely so the hadith is visibly set off from the Sheikh's own sentence. No word has been added or removed.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record.
